package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, when executed in a browser context, collects sensitive browser data including form inputs, credentials, and cookies. It exfiltrates this information to attacker-controlled endpoints via Telegram and Discord webhooks. The package masquerades as a simple wrapper for a legitimate utility, deceiving users and developers, and is linked to a known malicious author with a history of similar attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser context, upon import and function invocation)
execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (index.js or equivalent, top-level export)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the package is imported and its main function is called, the code imports and invokes a function from a related malicious package, processes the provided URL, and returns hardcoded author information along with the download result, maintaining the appearance of legitimate functionality.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code acts as a wrapper for a previously flagged malicious package, importing and executing its code under the guise of a legitimate utility. This serves as a smokescreen for deeper malicious activity and facilitates the delivery of additional malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate wrapper should not import or execute code from packages previously flagged as malicious, nor should it obfuscate its true purpose or include hardcoded author/contact information unrelated to the utility's function.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wrappers may call third-party utilities and return results, but not from known malicious sources or with embedded author contact details.
key_indicators: Wrapper function for a previously flagged malicious package
Obfuscated code structure in main export
Hardcoded author and contact information matching known malicious actors

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (obfuscated section, after initial import)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the page loads, the code selects all input and form elements in the DOM, attaches event listeners to monitor user interactions, and enables the capture of any data entered into forms.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Monitoring all form and input elements for changes is a common technique for harvesting sensitive user data, especially when performed by a third-party package without user awareness.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not globally monitor all form inputs unless explicitly designed as form analytics or accessibility tools, and even then, only with user consent and clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form analytics or accessibility tools may monitor form fields, but with user awareness, privacy safeguards, and opt-in consent.
key_indicators: Global event listeners on all form and input elements
No user notification or consent for data monitoring
Obfuscated implementation in main package file

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (obfuscated section, inside event listener)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
const data = {
    value: event.target.value,
    id: event.target.id,
    name: event.target.name,
    type: event.target.type,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    url: window.location.href,
    userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
    language: navigator.language,
    platform: navigator.platform,
    cookies: document.cookie
};
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, on every form input change event, the code collects the input value, metadata (id, name, type), timestamp, current URL, browser details, and all cookies, aggregating sensitive user and session information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting such a broad set of data, including cookies and browser environment details, is excessive for any legitimate form handler and is indicative of data theft and user tracking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate form handlers should only process necessary data and never access cookies or browser fingerprinting information without explicit user consent and a clear, documented purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may collect some metadata for fraud detection, but not cookies or full browser fingerprints, and only with user consent.
key_indicators: Collection of cookies and browser fingerprinting data
Harvesting of all form input values and metadata
No user notification or opt-in for data collection

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (obfuscated section, inside event listener)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a password field is changed, the code captures the password, the domain, and all other input values from the same form, ensuring full credential harvesting.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Capturing passwords and all associated form fields is a classic credential theft technique, especially when performed without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never access or transmit password fields or associated credentials unless explicitly authorized and for a clear, user-facing purpose, such as a password manager with explicit opt-in.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers may access password fields, but only with explicit user consent and local storage, never for exfiltration.
key_indicators: Harvesting of password fields and associated form data
Collection of all input values from the same form as the password
No user notification or opt-in for credential access

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (obfuscated section, exfiltration logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after sensitive data is collected, the code encodes the data and sends it via POST requests to multiple attacker-controlled endpoints (Telegram and Discord webhooks), ensuring exfiltration even if one endpoint is blocked.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating encoded user data to external endpoints, especially via popular messaging platforms, is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware and is designed to evade detection and blocking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not transmit user data to third-party endpoints without explicit user consent and clear documentation, and should never send sensitive credentials or cookies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some error reporting tools may send crash data, but never sensitive user credentials or cookies, and always with user opt-in.
key_indicators: Use of multiple exfiltration endpoints for redundancy
Use of Telegram and Discord as command-and-control (C2) channels

attack_chain.action: User installs and imports the imran-dlmedia package, which loads the wrapper and obfuscated malicious code.
Malicious code attaches event listeners to all form and input elements in the browser context to monitor user interactions.
On every form input change, the code collects input values, metadata, cookies, and browser fingerprinting data.
When a password field is detected, the code harvests the password and all associated form fields for comprehensive credential theft.
Collected data is encoded and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Telegram and Discord endpoints using POST requests.

behavioral_signatures: Global event listeners attached to all form and input elements in the DOM
Harvesting of password fields and all associated form data
Collection of cookies and browser fingerprinting data (userAgent, language, platform)
Encoding and exfiltration of user data to external endpoints via POST requests
Use of messaging platform APIs (Telegram, Discord) for data exfiltration
file_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript code in main package files (e.g., index.js)
References to nayan-video-downloader or nayan-media-downloader in require/import statements
Hardcoded author/contact information matching known malicious actors (e.g., 'MOHAMMAD IMRAN', Facebook/WhatsApp links)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that globally attach event listeners to all form or input elements, especially those that collect cookies, browser metadata, and password fields. Flag any code that encodes and POSTs user data to external endpoints, particularly to Telegram or Discord APIs. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated code and references to known malicious packages (nayan-video-downloader, nayan-media-downloader). Alert on any package that accesses document.cookie or navigator properties in the context of form handling, and on the presence of hardcoded author/contact information linked to known malicious actors.
